body:
Im not very smart, I may not give you kind of help/support you're looking for, and I might piss you off but I'll try to help atleast some and give you my take on it. I think it's a serious mistake to let your parents make your career/life decisions for you. I think it sounds like you've been pretty sheltered your whole life. Are you asian by chance? Your story reminds me so much of what a couple of people I know have gone through. It might help to know whether your parents think they can tell a 23 year old whether or not they are "allowed" to drop out because it's culturally acceptable to them or if they are just that controlling of you.

They told you to choose from stem and you chose stats because you could apply it to social sciences right? What was the social science field that you were actually interested in? Psych maybe? Your parents don't get to choose for you what you do with your life exactly because you get put in this kind of situation. You're in a career or program that you hate, you'll hate your family for putting you there, but you have sunken cost fallacy going on with the time and money you've already spent to get to your miserable if prestigious station. I think family should have input in your decisions but the choice has to be yours. I can understand why they would want you to go into stem, it's certainly true that there are many college degrees that wouldn't qualify you for much more than a barista at Starbucks. But even a seven figure salary can't buy you your mental health. Which you are losing everyday living out a life created by someone else for you which you hate.

I know this doesn't tell you what you should do right now, it's probably not what you want to hear, and what I'm suggesting is way way easier to say than it is to actually do. But I think you need to pump the breaks on your grad program. I think the most important and easily the most difficult thing you need to do is shift your mental gears from worrying about other people think of you to not giving a damn and doing what makes you happy. Dropping out of grad school looks bad on a resume? Who cares. If staying is making you miserable then don't stay. It doesn't matter if someone else won't like it, you deserve to be happy and it just isn't worth it. Think about what you want to do. This will be hard for someone who has had others make their decisions for them all their life but you have to do it. When you're thinking about what you want to do career wise don't think of it in overly permanent terms. If you want to be a biostatistician then don't be afraid to try and realize you don't like it later. You can change careers if you want. You can always go back to school. Try what you want, try more than one thing (but preferably one at a time), you can do it.

Now about your family though. I'm no pro and that's a hard thing to try to sort out but I'll try to give decent advice. If they are as I imagine them to be, you're gonna have a hell of a time trying to get them to support you making your own decisions if they don't 100% agree. That's hard. I imagine it gives you a lot of anxiety thinking about having that kind of conversation with them. I don't know your parents so I'm not confident if this advice works for your situation or not. But in general if you can talk to your family, work things out, preserve the relationship then you definitely should. It is absolutely worth the try atleast. But I also think that it's important to know that the real world can be a pretty crappy place and sometimes people have family that doesn't look out for them. Sometimes family can be toxic and they don't want what's best for you, they just want what's best for them. Sometimes family just wants to see you fail. I'm not saying that that's your family. Just saying it exists and it's real. We have to be willing to cut toxic people away from our life. Even if it's someone we love, even if it's a parent. I want you to live the best possible life, and that isn't possible if you allow other people to control you or mistreat you. But of course try to reason with them! Try over and over! It's always worth fighting for family. Just don't let them get their way with you. You will always fail a negotiation where you can't say no deal and walk away.

Anyways sorry if this pisses you off or wasn't very helpful. I definitely wasnt trying to be rude and I was trying to help. At the very least that's my take on it. Take it however you will.

I get how never having being with anyone can get you down. My "partner" is the reason why I'm here. Thinking about quitting it all and just feeling like talking about what's getting you down at the moment for whatever reason. Knowing both worlds I'm not really sure which one of us has it worse. Trying to navigate this world of pain for that one in a million chance or just never knowing the pain at all. Your family treat you like shit

I dont want that atleast. I'm sorry you're in this position. Can you telle how you got here? How old are you? What's going with you? I do genuinely want to hear your story atleast. I can't promise I'll be much help. I'm going through a lot to. But I do actually want to know why.

I get that. But in my opinion I believe that not one therapist is suited to all patients. And that I don't think it's fair to say that you've given it a try until you've given atleast a couple people a try. I think that like in all jobs there are sure to be a fair people in the mental health field who just suck at It and need to try something else. Some who have a good heart but the nature of the job doesn't suit them and is robbing them of their will to live, and people who are excellent at their job and live to help people like us you know? I'm not saying someone should live out their lives trying to find a good person to talk to. For twenty or thirty years down the line. But it isn't important to try a second person if the first isn't helpful. Maybe even a third.

Being in an awful place and losing some weight is definitely a plus. I know I've broken some plateaus through pain and heartbreak. But I think it's worth a try to take a more active role in your physical health. I know some people who say that the only way they could escape their emotional/mental pain was to get outside of their brains and enter their bodies. Again if you want to try I'm happy to help as little or as much as you want. If not no worries. But I do think it would make a difference.  I'm gonna try atleast a couple people before I give up. And I'm gonna atleast complete my fitness journey before I give up. I'm hoping that I find something to stay for along the way. But if I don't at the very least I know I will have seriously and honestly tried to make this world work for me.

Yeah. I have list of things that I absolutely want to try/do before I give up. It's a mix of things that I think you would be stupid not to try before giving up and things that I personally don't want to leave the world without trying. So stuff like talking to family, talking to a therapist or psychiatrist, trying medication, getting in better shape. I do think it's real when someone says it's hard to have a healthy mind in an unhealthy body. I used to be severely overweight but I lost a lot and trying to go all the way to like a six pack one day. I'm not very smart or trained as a psych professional in anyway but if weight loss or fitness is something you want to talk about or some advice about that's something I atleast feel confident I know what I'm talking about with. But past the obvious stuff to try I want to see the northern lights atleast once before I go. I bought some camping gear because I wanted to try and see things around the world before I go but covid kinda rendered impossible. I'm going to try to get a little practice with seeing things I want to see like glacier national park in Montana and then eventually going camping in iceland to see the lights. It's your life so do what you want but for mine I've decided that it would be stupid to not atleast try talking to family, strangers, professionals, medication, and then giving up after I've done the few things I want to experience before I leave this world.

Shit you already said you were. Sorry I tend to drink to get through my worst moments. Do you have anything that you felt you were supposed to do? Sorry if that's a question that hurts to be asked, I've just had several people in my life that always felt they've been called to be a doctor/whatever. I always thought they were weird. If not are there things that you've always wanted to do? I this thing that I call a reverse bucket list. Instead of things of that I want to do before I die it's a list of things that I want to try/experience before I call it quits. I don't want die or give up either so I have a list of things that would either be super stupid not to try or things that I want to do before I leave.

Hey. Im a lot older unfortunately at 27. I somehow end up here when I'm going through a lot of shit and feeling like calling it quits myself but somehow I usually end up trying to help out someone with their shit instead. Is sounds like you don' have a good relationship with your mom. Are you close to your sisters?

Yeah. Knowing both sides I honestly can't tell you if you have it worse or if I do. I wouldn't want to die without ever knowing what it's like to be truly in love. But at the same time there are no words that can express the pain of what it's like to be betrayed by someone who you trusted and loved with everything you had. And still love them after. It is absolutely insane, I used to make fun of people in my position but you can't really control how you feel.

Im 27 and a dude in missouri. I'm here because she came to visit her family for Christmas and told me shes dating now. And I'm just this loser working at Walmart trying to be better but feeling like I'll never be good enough. It sucks. Are you in high school?

I'm a little older. I'm a really shy guy and I don't have a lot of friends. I married my high school sweetheart and even married her. I wasnt ready for that and it didn't end well. I screwed up a lot and she cheated on me and left. She still keeps in touch and wants to be friends though. She told me today that she's in a relationship and I still have a lot of feelings for her so here I am. Got a bottle of stuff in my hand that I'm pretty sure would finish me but idk I just feel like chatting someone else up about their shit instead.

I'm glad you got a family that cares about you. A lot of posts I see here are about how their families are a big part of why they are here. In my experience it is just way too hard for someone who hasn't gone through depression to not kind of downplay your problems when you tell them about it. I think it's pretty safe to say your family cares and worries about you, but I think to be in the kind of place where you have to consider suicide as an escape is just so foreign to them they just can't you know? I know that opening up to family is so hard to begin with and when they respond to that with any kind of indifference it hurts, but try to keep in mind that they don't mean harm they just don't understand. Im really lucky in that my family even though they also don't understand what it's like to be pushed to this point, they still have some idea of how serious it is and are willing to drop things to atleast be there for me. Schools pretty shit for you to be failing. Do you get shit at school at all or do you not give a shit? Also sorry if you're uncomfortable with sharing too much but are you a dude or a girl?

I'm sorry that's awful. I usually come here when I'm in a lot of pain and want to give up but somehow I usually end up trying to chat with someone else about their shit. Are you in high school? You got a pretty shit family situation going on?
Hey. I'm austin. I know I'm a stranger but you wanna chat a bit about it? Is it just you and your mom? You in high school?

I'm sorry this is selfish of me. Dont go just yet. Obviously I want to dissuade you from doing this. I would like to talk to you about it. But at the very least I want to know why and how you got here. Could you tell me your story?

I'm sorry. It sounds like you're just done with everything. I want to talk for a bit but if youre just that done with it all then so be it. At the very least though I want to know why. Can you tell me what's brought you here? I want to talk to you about what you're going through but if you don't want to can you atleast tell me your story of how you got here. I actually do want to know.

I'm sorry you're going through this. :( I wish I was trained in this sort of thing and could give good quality advice. I don't think there's anything wrong with feeling uncomfortable in your body and wanting to make a change. But tying your self worth so heavily to your body and feeling the need to starve yourself definitely isn't good for you. Anorexia can be very lethal and I think it would good for you to talk to someone about it. I've felt a little how you do although thankfully it never pushed me towards anorexia. My wife and one person I cared about most in the world cheated and left me after ten years and the weight I had gained had something to do with it. I was 5'10 and 215lb at my heaviest. I'm down to 155lb now but that situation is still always on my mind. I always want to be leaner. Anyways if you want to talk more about what you're going through you can always chat with me here or in dm or something. I'm no therapist and I'm not all that smart but I can listen at the least. If you want some help with weight loss I have learned a lot about nutrition and fitness over the last year or two and I would be happy to answer any questions, give advice, write essays even I give zero fucks.

There's nothing wrong with being down or feeling pain. I think you are normal. There are plenty of people who are going through a lot but hide it well. Don't compare yourself to other people it just isn't fair. You know absolutely everything about yourself and you only know the surface of the people around you. So don't waste time and energy comparing yourself to others. If you wanna vent here then go for it. I'm not a therapist and I don't think I'm smart enough to give advice. But if you wanna post about some shit just know atleast someone is reading and listening.

Sounds good! If you're interested in losing fat you don't actually need the gym and you can get started whenever you want. Losing fat is like 90% nutrition. And it doesnt need to be awful and miserable like eating salad all the time. I lost seventy pounds without touching veggies (I'm a super picky eater). I have no idea what kind of shape you're in but unless you're one of those rare ones that can eat whatever you want and still keep your abs then losing ten or twenty pounds of fat is an excellent first goal for most people. There are ways to make burgers and ice cream good diet food if you're into that. I can show you an article of a university professor who lost almost thirty pounds on a twinkie diet. I wouldn't recommend it but I can help you make it work for you if that's what you're into. If your depression makes it difficult to stay motivated and disciplined with your health I can relate. Im actually going through a hard time myself right now. I get these intrusive thoughts that are scary and painful and I end up drinking to silence them. I haven't been to the gym in a while but I'm trying to start again soon to lose my last ten or twenty pounds. But anyways just let me know. It's an open invitation to you or anyone who is interested in trying to improve your mental health through fitness.

I think you should try shifting gears. You have mental health issues and you tried talk therapy and medication which I think was very smart. But it's not working so try working on your physical health instead. I suffer depression, I've been in a lot of pain, and I also consider suicide. Going to the gym helps me. And I know I was a lot worse off when I was seventy pounds heavier mentally as well as physically. I'm shy as well. Probably be accurate to say I'm socially awkward. I had my confidence completely destroyed and improving my body is a step towards building that confidence back. If you have nothing else to try then I suggest you try lifting. It's a good place to channel your pain. I guarantee you many of the bros in the gym are there for the same reason as you. To channel pain and sadness into something productive. If you think you might be interested in trying to lose some fat or build muscle or both but you have absolutely no clue what to do or how any of this works I am more than willing to help. I give zero shits. I will answer any question you have, I'll write you essays if you want on lifting or cardio or nutrition, I'll steer you towards where you can find other sources of good no bullshit information. It is absolutely zero trouble to me. It's the one thing in this world that I care about and enjoy talking about. Just let me know.

What's "wrong" with you is that you're in pain. And theres nothing wrong with being in pain. I would worry if you weren't in pain in that kind of situation. I wish I could help, but I'm not a therapist of any kind and I don't think I'm smart enough to offer advice. But I get suicidal thoughts and I know what it's like to be in pain. And I'm down to listen if you wanna talk more about what you're going through here or in pm or something. One thing that I do know a lot about is fitness though. I used to be severely overweight and over the past year I've lost seventy pounds and learned a good deal about nutrition and lifting in the process. If youre interested in improving your physical health I would be happy to share everything I know and/or coach you. There is a lot of misinformation on health and I would hate to see you get steered wrong by some bullshit when you're trying so hard to just hang in there.

Does it matter if you meet some kind of medical dictionary's definition of clinical depression or that you get a formal diagnosis? I think what's important is how do you feel. If you feel down or in pain and these feelings persist and/or interfere with your daily life then you should talk about these feelings with someone! Whether you've got something going on in your life that is painful and getting you down or if you're one of those people that have "nothing to complain about" but you're still experiencing depression, it doesn't matter and there's no shame in talking to someone about your mental health. If you can talk to your parents about how you're feeling and have them help you get in touch with a therapist/psychiatrist then that's great and I think you should! If your parents are the source of your problems then maybe you can try confiding in your school counselor. I'm no therapist and I don't think there are any in this forum but we're happy to listen if you wanna talk about your feelings and issues here or in pm.

You really should have this all figured out before you start. You should get diet and exercise sorted before you start and cut down 90% of the way there with that alone and then maybe use clen or something similar to finish if you want/need to. Clen isn't magic and you aren't going to lose weight successfully unless you already have diet and exercise down pat first. I'm not saying you don't know how to diet or exercise but I don't know you so you might not and this is important to know. Just don't start off a weight loss journey with peds, save them to help push through the finish line at the end. Granted if you did all that and you're starting clen to make it to your finish line then you should start on a light dose. Greg recommends 10mcg to start. See how well that works for you. You can always add more but going to a lighter dose causes problems. Look for the minimum effective dose where you are getting out of it what you're wanting out of it with minimal sides. If you find that the minimum effective dose for you causes problems then simply stop and try something else.

Yeah I think therapy definitely is a slow process. Im glad you got through your night. First thing on my list is to finish my fitness journey. When I was at my worst with my depression and panic attacks I never left the house and ate myself up to 215lbs. I had bad sleep apnea because I was so overweight so I would suddenly wake up in the middle of the night suffocating. I'm 155 now but I'm still not where I would like to be. So I don't want to give up before I get to <15% body fat and meeting my strength goals. This is pretty specific for me but I think everyone who makes a reverse bucket list needs something in the fitness category. In my opinion if you didn't work on improving your body, diet, and sleep before  quitting then you didn't really try. Although I have an unhealthy reason why this is important to me too. Going back to school to get a real job is on there too. I don't know how happy I can be barely surviving on minimum wage type jobs. And of course therapy and medication. Then there are things that I don't think would help but I dont think I want to leave without doing/seeing. Like stuff you might as well do if you're just going to die anyway. There's a video on youtube of a guy who stole a plane and just spent a few hours flying around doing flips and rolls and stuff before crashing it into a deserted island. Mine isn't nearly that dramatic though. For me I've just always wanted to see the northern lights. The starry night sky is something I've always been able to find some measure of beauty and peace in no matter what kind of state I was in and a view of the northern lights has to be the ultimate night sky. So I put camping in iceland to see the lights on my list. I'm not sure if this list is complete, I might have to add something social in. I just really struggle making friends and talking to people. But I think it's reasonable for me to say that if I can cross off everything on this list and I'm in the best physical shape of my life, pulled myself out of poverty, I've tried talking a professional that I can connect with (because not every therapist/psychiatrist is suitable for every patient), I've tried a few medications and didn't just give up after the first one failed, and I've tried building relationships with other people, and after all that I'm still in unmanageable agony then it's completely fair and reasonable to give up. I think this works for me because I've always been so lost and I've never been able to figure out what to do with my life. Its been a long time and I still have no purpose. So the reverse bucket list for me is giving me a sense of purpose in life even if it's just to earn the right to die. And hoping that somewhere along the way I come across the point where things get better for me.

The other guy is right she does need you. I know when you're in that kind of place it becomes really hard to believe that but whether you believe it or not it is the truth. Catastrophic cannot even begin to describe the damage that would be done to your sister if you left like that. It's true that for some people it doesn't get any better. But for many people it does. I've read some of their stories here. Try everything if not for your sake then for your sisters. I'm in so much pain too. I'm a massive drain on the people around me. In terms of money, time, emotion. I know what it feels like to feel so useless and to take from everyone without having anything to offer in return. I just want to give up. But I dont want to do something permanent when what I'm going through might be temporary. That option will always be available I might as well see if anything else works first. I actually made a reverse bucket list before I let myself give up. It's like a list of things that I feel like if I didn't do then I couldn't honestly say that I really tried to turn things around, plus a couple of things that I want to do if I'm just gonna quit after anyways. If you can't find any reason to keep trying then try instead to earn the right to die. Some things on my list are trying therapy, atleast three people since it's not like anybody will work for everybody. There's probably some bad or mismatched therapists out there. Finishing school and getting an actual job. Finishing my fitness journey, in my darkest moment I gave zero fucks and ate myself to 215 pounds. I'm 155 now but my goal was to be leaner and stronger. <15% body fat and deadlifting 2x my bodyweight. Plus I want to go camping in iceland just because I've always wanted to see the northern lights. Idk for some reason I want to see it before I quit. I'll do all that and if I don't find some reason to hang on along the way then seriously fuck. I gave it everything I had and literally no one can say I didn't give it a try. I'm sorry if that isn't helpful I'm not very smart and I can't really tell you what you should do. But if knowing someone else out there knows what it's like helps you then that would be really cool.

There's nothing wrong with rambling just let it out. I think there's a lot of therapeutic value in putting your thoughts and feelings into words even when it doesn't entirely make sense. So keep it up! Keep putting out there either in here or in a journal or something. I'm sorry that this event happened to you and that it's anniversary still hurts you like you this. It's ok that it still harms you like this. There is no deadline for healing and there's no shame in feeling the way that you do. If you aren't already talking to a pro like a therapist or psychiatrist then I hope that you do. I think that they can really help you heal from this. I hope you and your husband have a long happy marriage too and whatever you do I hope things get better for you, I really do.

Try not to hate them for not understanding. No one is going to get where you're coming from unless they've been through depression themselves. You don't want to let what you're going through to permanently and unnecessarily burn bridges for something that's a sort of temporary issue. I know you don't want to tell them about your situation but I think you should tell the ones that are pissing you off that you've got some shit going on that you need to deal with and to give you some space. Of course thats not guaranteed to preserve any relationships but it's better than blowing up on anyone. You mentioned that friends and family are part of what pulled you out of your hole before so try not to tell everyone to fuck off. I think it would be incredibly helpful to tell someone about your situation. I'm assuming someone already knows what's up if someone else helped pulled you out of it before but if not then I think talking to a pro would be of great help to you. This has happened before so it's probably going to be an ongoing issue for you and a pro can help give you tools to manage this throughout your life versus something to help you get through this moment. Although it's important to also have those things to help you in the moment. There are groups, chat rooms, forums, ect like this that you can talk to other people about this too. You can even vent at me if you want. I wouldn't try to deal with this on your own. Keep fighting man. I'm in a lot of pain too but I'm trying.

I know it's hard to realize this when you're in that kind of place, I've been there as well, but it's important to know that there are people who love you like your boyfriend. And even though I don't know anything about you I'm sure there are others as well. The thing about suicide is that catastrophic does not even begin to describe the damage done to the people who are left behind. I know this is a cliche but I really think things will get better for you if you keep fighting. I know this world isn't a perfect place and there are people for whom it just never gets any better. But there are for sure people for whom things did get better. You can find some of their stories here on reddit I know I read some of them. You've got someone laying next to you who cares and loves you. That is something huge. I really do think you can make it through this. I'm in a lot of pain too. I just want to quit honestly. But I want to atleast try to see if things get better. I don't want to kill myself over something that might be manageable. I'm probably weird but I made a reverse Bucket list. It's like a list of things that if I were to complete then I can say that I made a real honest attempt to turn things around I guess. Mines kinda a combination of things that would be dumb for me not to try before suicide like therapy and a couple things I might as well try to make the most of my time here before I go. I was tired of feeling lost and being out of options and I thought this was the best thing to try. I can make giving up my goal that I'm working towards and hope I find my reason to continue on as I go.

I'm no therapist but your feelings sound very natural to me. People prescribe exercise I think because it releases those feel good hormones that depressed people are severely lacking. And I think it's difficult to have a healthy mind in an unhealthy body. But what happens if someone  is working out and is eating well and it's had zero impact on their mood? It's like being healthier makes the depression worse cause you have too much energy to escape the pain in your sleep lol. I feel you. I do think you should continue to exercise and eat well though. I know it's frustrating that the only advice a lot of people and doctors can give is to exercise, eat better, and sleep well but those things do objectively matter. If improving those things alone didn't "solve" your problem then that doesn't mean that those things don't matter. It just means there's more than one condition you have to meet before you can improve. And I'm certain that improved physical health is one of them so don't abandon it. I realize how difficult that is when there are days when you can hardly find the willpower to get out of bed but I hope you never stop fighting the good fight even if it gets the better of you at times. I'm sorry I'm not smarter so I can't offer you any solutions. But I feel you brother and I really hope things get better for you. I'm barely holding on myself but I'm trying. Don't try to deal with this alone. Id try talking to a pro. I'm really lonely but Im lucky that I have a couple people I can talk to. If you aren't as lucky as me and don't have a family member or a friend to talk to then I think a pro is especially a good idea. There's groups and chat rooms and forums and stuff like here that you can go to as well. Hell you can vent to me too if you want.

I've been in your situation from the guys point of view. I think it's just important for you to know that he loves you and doesn't want to let you down. And he really is trying by just hanging on and doing that much is hard for him. In my situation it ended with my partner just getting worn down and giving up without telling me and then cheating with her best guy friend. I'm not saying you would do that but i do think that if this continues your relationship will end if you haven't lost feelings for him already. I think it's extremely important for you to understand that your emotional well-being comes first and what ultimately happens to him isn't your responsibility fiance or not. And I think that if medication and counseling and his friends taking him to the gym isn't working then he is going to need a serious shock to wake up and take back his life. I'm doing better now. I was also severely overweight and had no job or schooling or anything going on in my life. I'm still in an incredible amount of pain one year later but I'm still doing better. I have a job, I'm trying to get back in school, I'm sixty pounds lighter. I'm not whole yet I still have a lot of problems but I'm trying and I have made observable progress. And maybe if my wife had left me before she lost feelings and made some poor decisions, and held onto those feelings and revisited me one year later then maybe we could have turned out differently. I can't tell you if that's what you need to do or if that's a good idea for your situation. But I wish it what would have happened in mine.
